title: Tempo
description: A metronome reduced to its dial: one large number on black and, beneath it, a calibrated ruler of fine ticks with a small figure under every tenth. Scroll, swipe or drag and the ruler streams past a fixed centre mark with real momentum, settling into a detent on every whole beat per minute while the digits roll over like a mechanical counter. The centre mark is the only thing printed in a second ink, a vermilion, and it is the metronome's pallet: on every beat it kicks to the ruler's full height and a heavier stroke, then sinks back to a tick's length, and after the first touch a soft synthesized click keeps time with it. Tap to silence it.
intent: From Rauno Freiberg's Wheel input (https://rauno.me/craft/wheel-input): a numeric input changed by direct manipulation with the scroll gesture, ticks passing under a fixed needle, updated through refs so it never lags. Here the value is a tempo, so the number can also be heard and seen keeping time.
